entries.name: AWID3 (Aegean Wi-Fi Intrusion Dataset v3)
entries.description: 802.11 attacks under WPA2-Enterprise with PMF enabled (deauth, evil twin, KRACK-style, Krook, and others) plus higher-layer attacks (SQLi, SSH brute force, botnet, website spoofing, malware). Raw cleartext PCAPs and the AWID3-CSV with 254 features.

entries.known_limitations: No licence. Derived from small lab sets.
entries.attribution: Shafi, Habibi Lashkari, Mohanty, Computers and Electrical Engineering 2024
entries.recommended_use: Unified DNS feature set. Prefer the CIC originals because their terms are clearer.
entries.notes: Request form only, no licence visible.

entries.name: BCCC-CIC-IDS2017
entries.description: CIC-IDS2017 raw PCAPs re-processed with NTLFlowLyzer (network and transport-layer features) into new CSVs with sub-categorised attack labels.
entries.label_quality: Re-extracted by the original CIC author group. I found no independent audit.
entries.known_limitations: Same synthetic testbed as CIC-IDS2017. No licence text.
entries.attribution: Shafi, Habibi Lashkari, Haghighian Roudsari, 'NTLFlowLyzer...', Computers & Security 104160, 2024
entries.recommended_use: Alternative feature set for CIC-IDS2017.

entries.name: BCCC-CIRA-CIC-DoHBrw-2020 (balanced)
entries.description: Balanced version of DoHBrw-2020 with equal malicious and benign DoH instances, produced with SMOTE oversampling. Three CSVs (malicious, benign, combined).

entries.label_quality: Balanced with SMOTE, so part of the minority class is synthetic. Do not use it for test splits.
entries.known_limitations: SMOTE samples leak across splits and inflate metrics.

entries.recommended_use: Prefer the original DoHBrw-2020 and balance it yourself.
entries.notes: Request form only, no licence visible.

entries.description: Enhanced CSE-CIC-IDS2018: labels aligned to attacker IPs instead of timestamps, UDP attacks misclassified by TCP-specific analysis removed, and features re-extracted with NTLFlowLyzer.

entries.recommended_use: Large flow-feature benchmark with corrected labels.
entries.notes: Access is by request form only, and no licence is visible.

entries.name: Bot-IoT
entries.description: Simulated IoT network with normal and botnet traffic: DDoS and DoS (by protocol), OS and service scans, keylogging and data exfiltration. PCAP, Argus and CSV, plus a 5% extract.

entries.label_quality: Testbed ground truth. Overwhelmingly attack traffic, with very few normal records (widely reported; not re-verified).
entries.known_limitations: Extreme imbalance. Simulated.
entries.attribution: Koroniotis, Moustafa, Sitnikova, Turnbull, Future Generation Computer Systems 100 (2019) 779-796, plus other listed papers
entries.recommended_use: Academic benchmark.
entries.notes: The download link is a UNSW SharePoint link and was not extracted.

entries.name: CAIDA Anonymized Internet Traces (passive_dataset)
entries.geographic_coverage: US backbone links (Equinix Chicago, San Jose, NYC monitors)
entries.description: Anonymised packet-header traces from high-speed commercial backbone links, Apr 2008 to Jan 2019.
entries.label_quality: Unlabelled.

entries.name: CIC-Bell-DNS-2021
entries.organisation: Canadian Institute for Cybersecurity, UNB with Bell Canada
entries.geographic_coverage: Domains from global blocklists; benign domains from Majestic Million
entries.description: DNS traffic and features for benign, malware, spam and phishing domains. Domains were requested over HTTP, DNS packets were captured, and lexical plus DNS-response features were extracted.
entries.records: Domains processed / packets processed: malware 9,432 / 182,266; spam 1,976 / 61,046; phishing 12,586 / 95,492; benign 500,000 / 6,907,719 (Table 2 on the page)
entries.label_quality: Labels come from source blocklists, and only domains that responded HTTP 200 were kept. The page does not name the source feeds' terms. I did not verify labels beyond that.
entries.known_limitations: Many malicious domains were already dead, which biases the set toward still-live infrastructure. Benign set comes from Majestic Million (CC BY 3.0 according to Tranco).
entries.attribution: Mahdavifar, Maleki, Habibi Lashkari, Broda, Razavi, 'Classifying Malicious Domains using DNS Traffic Analysis', IEEE DASC 2021
entries.recommended_use: Malicious-domain classification from DNS features. Check upstream blocklist provenance first.
entries.notes: UNB CIC FAQ (datasets index page), answering the question 'What is your policy of using your dataset collections by private companies, for commercial use?', says: 'You may redistribute, republish, and mirror our datasets in any form; however, any use or redistribution of the data must include a citation to the dataset and the research paper listed on the webpage.' This is permissive in practice but is not a formal licence and does not expressly grant commercial or model-training rights, so it is classed RESEARCH/unclear. Get written confirmation from CIC before commercial training. Upstream blocklist sources may have their own terms, not checked here.

entries.organisation: Canadian Institute for Cybersecurity, UNB with Bell Canada
entries.description: DNS data-exfiltration dataset: light and heavy exfiltration of various file types over DNS, plus benign DNS traffic. Stateless and stateful DNS features.

This is permissive in practice but is not a formal licence and does not expressly grant commercial or model-training rights, so it is classed RESEARCH/unclear. entries.name: CIC-DDoS2019
entries.description: Reflection and exploitation DDoS attacks (NTP, DNS, LDAP, MSSQL, NetBIOS, SNMP, SSDP, UDP, UDP-Lag, WebDDoS, SYN, TFTP, PortMap) over 2 days, with B-Profile benign background. PCAPs plus CICFlowMeter-V3 CSVs.
entries.collection_period: 2 capture days (training day and testing day; exact dates not re-read)
entries.label_quality: Labels are by time window and IP. CICFlowMeter issues similar to those documented for CIC-IDS2017 are likely (inference, not verified for this dataset).
entries.known_limitations: Very imbalanced, with attack traffic dominating. WebDDoS volume is very low. PortScan appears only on the test day.
entries.attribution: Sharafaldin, Habibi Lashkari, Hakak, Ghorbani, IEEE ICCST 2019
entries.recommended_use: Training signal for edge detection of DNS, NTP and SSDP amplification.
entries.notes: UNB CIC FAQ (datasets index page), answering the question 'What is your policy of using your dataset collections by private companies, for commercial use?', says: 'You may redistribute, republish, and mirror our datasets in any form; however, any use or redistribution of the data must include a citation to the dataset and the research paper listed on the webpage.' This is permissive in practice but is not a formal licence and does not expressly grant commercial or model-training rights, so it is classed RESEARCH/unclear. Get written confirmation from CIC before commercial training.

entries.name: CIC-IDS2017 (Intrusion Detection Evaluation Dataset)
entries.organisation: Canadian Institute for Cybersecurity, University of New Brunswick
entries.geographic_coverage: Lab testbed (synthetic, Fredericton CA); not geo-representative
entries.description: 5 days of testbed traffic (benign B-Profile users + brute force, DoS/DDoS, Heartbleed, web attacks, infiltration, Ares botnet, port scans). Full PCAPs plus CICFlowMeter labelled flows (80+ features).
entries.records: Flow count not stated on the dataset page. Daily PCAP sizes on the page are 11.0, 11, 13, 7.8 and 8.3 GB, about 51 GB in total.
entries.label_quality: Poor in the original CSVs. Engelen et al. 2021 (WTMC/IEEE SPW) reconstructed or relabelled more than 20% of traces after finding flow-construction, feature and labelling bugs. Liu et al. 2022 (IEEE CNS) and Lanvin et al. 2022 (CRiSIS) found more labelling errors and duplicate or misordered packets.
entries.known_limitations: Synthetic and small (about 25 simulated users). CICFlowMeter artefacts such as TCP teardown flows. Labelling uses time windows. Several attack classes are trivially separable. Use the DistriNet-corrected version, not the original CSVs.
entries.attribution: Sharafaldin, Habibi Lashkari, Ghorbani, 'Toward Generating a New Intrusion Detection Dataset and Intrusion Traffic Characterization', ICISSP 2018
entries.recommended_use: Use only as a baseline benchmark, through the corrected DistriNet relabel. Do not use it as the main source of training signal.
entries.notes: The licence section on the dataset page only says the data is 'publicly available for researchers' and asks for citation of the ICISSP paper. UNB CIC FAQ (datasets index page), answering the question 'What is your policy of using your dataset collections by private companies, for commercial use?', says: 'You may redistribute, republish, and mirror our datasets in any form; however, any use or redistribution of the data must include a citation to the dataset and the research paper listed on the webpage.' This is permissive in practice but is not a formal licence and does not expressly grant commercial or model-training rights, so it is classed RESEARCH/unclear. Get written confirmation from CIC before commercial training. The download link leads to a registration form. Kaggle re-uploads carry conflicting licence fields (chethuhn/network-intrusion-dataset says 'CC0: Public Domain'; dhoogla/cicids2017 says 'CC BY-NC-SA 4.0'). Neither overrides UNB's terms.

entries.name: CICIoT2023
entries.description: 33 attacks in 7 categories (DDoS, DoS, Recon, Web-based, Brute Force, Spoofing, Mirai) run by malicious IoT devices against other IoT devices in a 105-device topology. PCAPs plus DPKT-extracted CSV features.
entries.label_quality: Per-attack captures, so labels are file-level. I found no published audit.
entries.known_limitations: Mostly volumetric attacks. Features are windowed packet aggregates rather than standard flows.
entries.attribution: Neto, Dadkhah, Ferreira, Zohourian, Lu, Ghorbani, 'CICIoT2023...', Sensors 2023
entries.recommended_use: IoT and edge-router attack detection (Mirai, DDoS), relevant for home gateways.
entries.notes: UNB CIC FAQ (datasets index page), answering the question 'What is your policy of using your dataset collections by private companies, for commercial use?', says: 'You may redistribute, republish, and mirror our datasets in any form; however, any use or redistribution of the data must include a citation to the dataset and the research paper listed on the webpage.' This is permissive in practice but is not a formal licence and does not expressly grant commercial or model-training rights, so it is classed RESEARCH/unclear. Get written confirmation from CIC before commercial training. The dataset page has no licence block. Record count is not on the page.

entries.name: CIRA-CIC-DoHBrw-2020

entries.description: Daily top 1M most-queried domains (including subdomains) from Umbrella passive DNS, plus a top-TLD list. Historical lists are at top-1m-YYYY-MM-DD.csv.zip.
entries.records: 1,000,000 domains per list. Zip is 12,761,265 bytes, Last-Modified Wed, 18 Nov 2026 01:17:32 GMT (HTTP HEAD on 2026-11-18).
entries.label_quality: Popularity only. Includes infrastructure, tracking and some malicious or abused domains.
entries.known_limitations: DNS-popularity based, so it contains CDN, telemetry and possibly malicious high-volume domains. Needs filtering.
entries.recommended_use: DNS-centric benign baseline, which fits HookProbe's DNS view better than web-centric lists. Get Cisco's terms before commercial use.
entries.notes: Still live and updated daily as of 2026-11-18. No licence grant was found, and the copyright notice suggests all rights reserved.

entries.name: CSE-CIC-IDS2018 (IPS/IDS dataset on AWS)
entries.organisation: Communications Security Establishment (CSE) and Canadian Institute for Cybersecurity, UNB
entries.description: Large AWS testbed (5 subnets, 420 machines and 30 servers according to the page) with 7 attack scenarios: brute force, Heartbleed, botnet, DoS, DDoS, web attacks, infiltration. PCAPs, Windows/Ubuntu event logs, and CICFlowMeter-V3 CSVs.
entries.collection_period: 2018 (attack days in Feb-Mar 2018; exact dates not re-read on page)
entries.label_quality: Known errors (Liu et al. 2022, IEEE CNS). DoS labels were wrong because labelling used timestamps. BCCC re-labelled by attacker IP, and DistriNet re-labelled as well.
entries.known_limitations: Synthetic. Labelling errors. Very large, with heavy class imbalance.
entries.attribution: cite CSE-CIC-IDS2018 and link the AWS registry page; Sharafaldin et al. ICISSP 2018
entries.recommended_use: Large-volume flow benchmark. Prefer the BCCC or DistriNet relabels.
entries.notes: UNB CIC FAQ (datasets index page), answering the question 'What is your policy of using your dataset collections by private companies, for commercial use?', says: 'You may redistribute, republish, and mirror our datasets in any form; however, any use or redistribution of the data must include a citation to the dataset and the research paper listed on the webpage.' This is permissive in practice but is not a formal licence and does not expressly grant commercial or model-training rights, so it is classed RESEARCH/unclear. Get written confirmation from CIC before commercial training. Public S3 bucket, no sign-in needed. Kaggle re-upload solarmainframe/ids-intrusion-csv is labelled 'CC BY 4.0' by the uploader, which does not override CIC's terms.

entries.name: HTTP DATASET CSIC 2010
entries.organisation: Information Security Institute, CSIC (Spanish National Research Council)
entries.description: Automatically generated HTTP requests to a web shop: a normal-only training set, a normal test set and an anomalous test set (SQLi, buffer overflow, CRLF, XSS, parameter tampering, and others).
entries.records: About 36,000 normal and more than 25,000 anomalous requests (secondary, from search summary of the official page)
entries.label_quality: Generated, with labels by construction. The generation method is not precisely documented (literature).
entries.known_limitations: Old (2010). Single synthetic application. Not representative of modern web traffic.
entries.attribution: citation expected; exact text not verified
entries.recommended_use: WAF-style HTTP anomaly baseline for research only.
entries.notes: The official page (tic.itefi.csic.es, a CNAME to www.isi.csic.es) timed out from this host, so I could not read licence terms. The Kaggle mirror ispangler/csic-2010-web-application-attacks lists its licence as 'Data files © Original Authors', meaning no grant.

entries.name: CTU-13 botnet dataset
entries.organisation: Stratosphere Laboratory, Czech Technical University in Prague
entries.description: 13 scenarios, each with real botnet malware (Neris, Rbot, Virut, Murlo, Menti, Sogou, NSIS.ay) running inside a real university network with normal and background traffic. Manually labelled bidirectional Argus NetFlows. Botnet-only PCAPs and malware binaries are included.
entries.records: 13 scenarios; full archive 1.9 GB (CTU-13 page); per-scenario NetFlow and label counts in Tables 3-4 on the page (not transcribed)
entries.label_quality: Manual flow-by-flow labelling. Background traffic is labelled 'Background', meaning unknown and not guaranteed benign. The authors say the original unidirectional NetFlows should not be used.
entries.known_limitations: Dated (2011, Windows XP-era bots). Full mixed PCAPs are withheld for privacy. Background traffic is unlabelled.
entries.attribution: Garcia, Grill, Stiborek, Zunino, 'An empirical comparison of botnet detection methods', Computers & Security 45 (2014) 100-123
entries.recommended_use: C2 and botnet flow-behaviour training with real background traffic. Treat 'Background' as unlabelled.
entries.notes: The datasets overview page says 'The CTU-13 dataset is published with the license Creative Commons CC-BY' and links CC BY 2.0. The FAQ says no permission is needed if cited. personal_data is a judgement: real university hosts are present, but I did not verify whether IPs were anonymised. The archive contains live malware binaries, so handle it in a sandbox. 2026-11-21: mcfp.felk.cvut.cz timed out on 80/443, so the 12 labelled bidirectional NetFlow files (capture*.binetflow.xz) were taken from the backup mirror the CTU-13 page links (https://mega.nz/#F!vdRmBA6D). Only those files and the READMEs were downloaded: no pcaps, no malware archives. Every file matched the size the mirror listed and decompressed with valid xz checksums; there is no official hash to compare against. The mirror has no binetflow for scenario 10 (CTU-Malware-Capture-Botnet-51, only pcaps and rbot.exe.zip), so scenario 10 is missing. Scenario n = capture 41+n. The mirror READMEs carry no licence statement; the CC BY terms come from the Stratosphere datasets overview page.

entries.name: CVE List (CVE JSON 5.x records)
entries.organisation: CVE Program (MITRE as Secretariat; sponsored by CISA)
entries.description: Authoritative CVE records published by CNAs, mirrored to GitHub with hourly deltas.
entries.records: 430075 vulnerabilities from the CVE Program (vulnerability.circl.lu/about sources list, 2026-11-21); cvelistv5.ndjson was 6,461,066,392 bytes on 2026-11-21
entries.update_frequency: repo updated ~every 7 minutes; hourly delta zips; daily baseline
entries.known_limitations: Quality of CNA data varies; no exploitation signal on its own.
entries.attribution: Reproduce MITRE's copyright designation and the CVE Terms of Use licence (per SPDX cve-tou).
entries.recommended_use: fine-tune vulnerability knowledge; local CVE enrichment on device
entries.notes: Terms re-verified 2026-11-21 from the CVE website source (TermsOfUse.vue in CVEProject/cve-website): MITRE grants a perpetual, worldwide, non-exclusive, no-charge, royalty-free, irrevocable copyright licence to reproduce, prepare derivative works of, display, sublicense and distribute CVE, provided MITRE's copyright designation and the licence are reproduced in copies. vulnerability.circl.lu labels the CVE Program source 'CC BY 4.0'; the CVE ToU is the governing text and is what the registry records. Acquired from CIRCL Vulnerability-Lookup's daily NDJSON dump (one CVE JSON 5 record per line), which mirrors cvelistV5. Records can carry ADP containers: CISA-ADP (Vulnrichment, CC0) and the CVE Program container.

entries.name: Improved CIC-IDS2017 and CSE-CIC-IDS2018 (WTMC2021 / CNS2022 relabels)
entries.geographic_coverage: Same testbeds as the CIC originals
entries.description: Fully re-extracted (fixed CICFlowMeter) and relabelled versions of CIC-IDS2017 and CSE-CIC-IDS2018 with reverse-engineered, published labelling logic and an 'Attempted' label for attack flows that carry no malicious behaviour.
entries.label_quality: Best available for these two datasets. Labelling code is public (GitHub GintsEngelen/WTMC2021-Code). The authors say 'Attempted' flows should be merged into Benign or the attack class and never used as a separate class.
entries.known_limitations: Inherits the synthetic-testbed limits of the originals. No licence of its own.
entries.attribution: Engelen, Rimmer, Joosen, IEEE SPW 2021; Liu, Engelen, Lynar, Essam, Joosen, IEEE CNS 2022; plus the original CIC papers
entries.recommended_use: Preferred replacement for the original CIC-IDS2017 and CSE-CIC-IDS2018 CSVs in benchmarks.
entries.notes: The download page text was read, but the actual file host link and file sizes were not checked. The pages give no licence. Lanvin et al. 2022 (CRiSIS, 'Errors in the CICIDS2017 dataset...', HAL hal-03775466) also publish a critique, but I could not find a download location for their corrected data. The DistriNet hosts did not resolve on the local resolver and were reached via public DNS.

entries.name: DNS Threats Dataset (normal / DGA / tunnelling domains)
entries.organisation: Stratosphere Lab (CTU) and UNCuyo / CONICET (Palau, Catania, Guerra, Garcia, Rigaki)
entries.description: Domain-name dataset with 3 classes (0 normal, 1 DGA, 2 tunnelling). Normal: Alexa top 1M, 3,161 Bambenek normal domains and 177,017 others. DGA: 51 families from Abakumov and Bambenek repositories. Tunnelling: 8,000 domains from iodine, dnscat2 and dnsExfiltrator.
entries.records: Files: train_combined_multiclass.csv.gz 23,030,305 bytes; test_combined_multiclass.csv.gz 6,326,259 bytes (Zenodo API). Row count not read.
entries.label_quality: Labels come from source lists. The tunnelling class is lab-generated with only 3 tools.
entries.known_limitations: Upstream sources carry their own terms: Alexa (discontinued, proprietary), Bambenek feeds (commercial terms not verified here), and the Abakumov DGA repo.
entries.attribution: Palau, Catania, Guerra, García, Rigaki, 'Detecting DNS threats: A deep learning model to rule them all', ASAI 2019 / JAIIO 48
entries.recommended_use: Multiclass DNS domain classifier prototyping. Commercial use depends on upstream clearance.
entries.notes: The CC BY 3.0 US grant is explicit, so the class is OPEN, but commercial_use is marked unclear. The depositors can only license what they own, and the dataset repackages Alexa and Bambenek lists, whose terms were not cleared. The tunnelling subset (lab-generated by the authors) is the cleanest part.

entries.attribution: Apache-2.0 NOTICE; upstream CVE Terms of Use attribution (not re-read in this session)

entries.notes: Derived from CVE feeds. The CVE ToU is permissive but needs attribution. I did not re-read it in this session. Licence field from the HF dataset card YAML.

entries.name: CTIBench
entries.organisation: AI4Sec (Rochester Institute of Technology; Alam et al.)
entries.description: CTI benchmark for LLMs: CTI-MCQ, CTI-RCM (CVE to CWE root-cause mapping), CTI-VSP (CVSS prediction), CTI-ATE (ATT&CK technique extraction) and CTI-TAA (threat actor attribution).
entries.records: Size category 1K<n<10K (card YAML)
entries.label_quality: Curated benchmark answers.
entries.known_limitations: Evaluation set only. Training on it contaminates evaluation.
entries.attribution: CC BY; cite the CTIBench paper
entries.recommended_use: Internal evaluation only. Do not train on it.
entries.notes: Non-commercial share-alike. Mirrors (e.g. RISys-Lab/Benchmarks_CyberSec_CTI-Bench, tagged cc-by-sa-4.0) do not override the original NC term. Licence field from the HF dataset card YAML.

entries.name: CyberMetric
entries.organisation: Tihanyi, Ferrag, Jain, Bisztray, Debbah (TII / Khalifa University and collaborators)
entries.description: 10,000 cybersecurity multiple-choice questions generated with LLMs via RAG over standards and docs, verified by human experts. Subsets of 80, 500, 2,000 and 10,000.
entries.records: 10,000 questions (dataset card)
entries.label_quality: LLM-generated and human-verified per the card.
entries.known_limitations: Benchmark. Training on it contaminates evaluation. Generated with third-party LLMs.
entries.recommended_use: Held-out knowledge evaluation for the security model.
entries.notes: Apache-2.0, but it is generated with LLMs whose terms may restrict using outputs to train competing models. Treat it as an evaluation set. Licence field from the HF dataset card YAML.

entries.name: ealvaradob/phishing-dataset (combined URLs, emails, SMS, HTML)
entries.description: Compilation of 4 phishing sources (Kaggle email set incl. Enron, Kaggle SMS, Kaggle 800k URL set, Mendeley 80k website HTML set) into text and label pairs.
entries.records: Size category 10K<n<100K (card YAML)
entries.label_quality: Inherited from the 4 sources, then deduplicated and balanced.
entries.known_limitations: Aggregates sources with different and unknown licences.
entries.recommended_use: Do not use for commercial training until each upstream source is cleared. It is a licence-laundering example.
entries.notes: The aggregator relabelled third-party Kaggle and Mendeley data as Apache-2.0. A re-uploader cannot grant more rights than the sources do. The email content (Enron-derived) contains real personal data. Licence field from the HF dataset card YAML.

entries.name: Cybersecurity-Dataset-Fenrir v2.1
entries.description: Defensive security SFT triples (OWASP, MITRE ATT&CK, NIST CSF, CIS, cloud and DevSecOps, crypto, AI security) with built-in refusal patterns.
entries.records: 99,870 rows (dataset card)
entries.label_quality: LLM-aided generation from '450k+ public technical docs' per the card, with dedup and hallucination scans claimed.
entries.known_limitations: Single-author dataset. Source documents are not listed. The 'licensing respected' claim cannot be audited.
entries.recommended_use: Supplementary SFT data, filtered.
entries.notes: Card claims 'Commercial-friendly' and 'Only public sources; licensing respected'. Licence field from the HF dataset card YAML. Derived content from vendor whitepapers may not be Apache-compatible.

entries.name: NIST Cybersecurity Training Dataset v1.1
entries.description: Text chunks and QA extracted (Docling) from NIST CSRC publications (SP 800 series, CSWP, and others) for fine-tuning and RAG. Includes OpenAI text-embedding-3-small embeddings.
entries.records: Size category 100K<n<1M (card YAML)
entries.label_quality: Extracted text with good provenance (NIST publication per record).
entries.known_limitations: Compliance-oriented rather than detection. The embeddings were produced with an OpenAI model, so check whether the embedding columns are needed.
entries.recommended_use: Clean-provenance policy and controls knowledge for SOC-assistant RAG and SFT.
entries.notes: The CC0 claim relies on US-government works being public domain in the US. NIST SPs that reproduce third-party material may contain copyrighted excerpts. Licence field from the HF dataset card YAML.

entries.name: Trendyol Cybersecurity Defense Instruction-Tuning Dataset v2.0
entries.description: System/user/assistant instruction-tuning examples covering more than 200 defensive security topics (IR, threat hunting, cloud, OT/ICS, MITRE ATT&CK, NIST mapping).
entries.records: 53,202 rows (dataset card)
entries.label_quality: Unverified synthetic or curated answers. The card mentions '500K+ sources' and hallucination checks but gives no source list or generator model.
entries.known_limitations: Provenance is opaque. Content is likely LLM-generated, and the generating model's terms are unknown.
entries.recommended_use: SOC-reasoning SFT seed after dedup and quality filtering. Record the provenance risk.
entries.notes: Apache-2.0 per card. Licence field from the HF dataset card YAML. The card does not disclose source documents or the generating LLM, so the upstream licence chain cannot be verified.

entries.name: WitFoo Precinct6 Cybersecurity Dataset v2.1.0
entries.description: Sanitised real SOC telemetry: live security events from 4 organisations labelled malicious, suspicious or benign, with 51,371 incident provenance graphs, embedded triggering signals, MITRE technique mapping and natural-language attack reports. A 100M-row sibling exists.
entries.records: 2,011,674 live signals (2024-07-26 to 2024-08-01) and 238,511 embedded incident signals (2022-05-30 to 2024-07-28); merged graph 47,585 nodes and 1,740,438 edges (dataset card)
entries.label_quality: Labels come from WitFoo Precinct correlation (incident leads), not analyst ground truth. v2.1 fixed timeline separation, timestamps and uuid corruption after the University of Canterbury evaluation.
entries.known_limitations: Vendor-pipeline labels. Earlier versions let some values escape sanitisation (card admits device and account names survived in escaped JSON).
entries.recommended_use: Rare openly licensed real SOC triage and provenance data. Run your own PII scan before use.
entries.notes: Real customer data released by the vendor under Apache-2.0. Whether WitFoo had the right to release it under customer contracts is not verifiable, and residual-PII history suggests caution (GDPR, if any EU data). Licence field from the HF dataset card YAML.

entries.name: HookProbe synthetic SOC triage templates
entries.description: Template-generated triage examples (tools/intel-data/heqkdata/builders.py SOC_SCENARIOS), malicious and benign twins of the heqk rule categories. Explicitly synthetic.
entries.records: 36 (9 scenarios x 4)
entries.label_quality: synthetic; illustrative only
entries.known_limitations: Written by the same author as the pipeline; teaches format, not real-world distributions.
entries.recommended_use: format teaching and pipeline tests; never evidence

entries.name: Infection Monkey
entries.description: Open-source breach and attack simulation tool.
entries.recommended_use: lab-only traffic generation

entries.name: IoT-23 (Aposemat)
entries.organisation: Stratosphere Laboratory, CTU Prague (funded by Avast)
entries.description: 23 captures: 20 malware scenarios (Mirai, Okiru, Torii, Hajime, Gafgyt, and others) run on IoT devices, and 3 benign real IoT device captures (Philips Hue, Amazon Echo, Somfy lock). Zeek conn.log files with labels and detailed labels such as PartOfAHorizontalPortScan, C&C, DDoS and FileDownload.
entries.records: 20 malicious and 3 benign scenarios. Malicious label counts include PartOfAHorizontalPortScan 213,852,924, Okiru 47,381,241 and DDoS 19,538,713 flows (IoT-23 page). Full archive 21,510,801,277 bytes (Zenodo); flows-only archive 8.8 GB (page).
entries.label_quality: Semi-automatic rule-based labels (manual analysis, the labelling spreadsheet, and the Flaber tool). Heavily dominated by port-scan flows.
entries.known_limitations: Extreme imbalance. Few benign devices (3 captures). Malware runs are long with repetitive traffic.
entries.attribution: Garcia, Parmisano, Erquiaga (2020). IoT-23: A labeled dataset with malicious and benign IoT network traffic (v1.0.0). Zenodo. doi:10.5281/zenodo.4743746
entries.recommended_use: Primary open-licensed IoT botnet and C2 training source for edge gateways. Deduplicate and rebalance the port-scan flows.
entries.notes: The Zenodo record license field is cc-by-4.0, and access_right is open. The Stratosphere page has no separate licence block. personal_data is set to none because the benign captures come from lab devices (judgement).

entries.name: IPinfo Lite
entries.description: Free country + ASN database and API.
entries.recommended_use: ASN/country enrichment (attribution + share-alike).
entries.notes: 'Released under Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0'; FAQ: may 'freely use and incorporate the data into commercial and non-commercial applications'; attribution required. Token/signup needed. Check SA obligations for redistributed derivatives. API: https://api.ipinfo.io/lite/{ip}?token=... (per page example).

entries.name: IPsum threat-IP aggregate
entries.description: Daily list of suspicious/malicious IPs scored by number of blocklists they appear on.
entries.recommended_use: Reputation feature (blocklist-hit count) after upstream review.
entries.notes: Repo Unlicense, but list is derived from 30+ third-party blocklists whose terms (e.g. abuse.ch, Spamhaus) restrict commercial/AI use - treat as unclear.

entries.name: IPtoASN database
entries.description: IP range -> ASN, country, AS description; IPv4/IPv6/combined, updated hourly.
entries.recommended_use: On-device IP->ASN enrichment and ASN-level features.
entries.notes: 'Licensed under Public Domain (PDDL v1.0)'; 'Updated hourly'. Good open replacement for Team Cymru lookups.

entries.name: ISCX-URL2016
entries.description: Benign, spam, phishing, malware and defacement URLs with lexical features, built for malicious-URL and obfuscation analysis.
entries.records: About 35,300 benign (Alexa), about 12,000 spam (WEBSPAM-UK2007), about 10,000 phishing (OpenPhish), more than 11,500 malware (DNS-BH) and more than 45,450 defacement URLs (dataset page)
entries.label_quality: Labels are inherited from the source feeds. Benign URLs were checked with VirusTotal.
entries.known_limitations: Stale (2016). Benign set comes from Alexa, which is discontinued. Derived from third-party feeds (OpenPhish, DNS-BH, WEBSPAM-UK2007) with their own terms.
entries.attribution: Mamun, Rathore, Habibi Lashkari, Stakhanova, Ghorbani, 'Detecting Malicious URLs Using Lexical Analysis', NSS 2016
entries.recommended_use: Lexical URL baseline only. Too old for production training.
entries.notes: UNB CIC FAQ (datasets index page), answering the question 'What is your policy of using your dataset collections by private companies, for commercial use?', says: 'You may redistribute, republish, and mirror our datasets in any form; however, any use or redistribution of the data must include a citation to the dataset and the research paper listed on the webpage.' This is permissive in practice but is not a formal licence and does not expressly grant commercial or model-training rights, so it is classed RESEARCH/unclear. Get written confirmation from CIC before commercial training. Redistribution is marked unclear because the content is third-party feed data, such as OpenPhish, whose commercial feed is paid.

entries.name: JVN iPedia / MyJVN API
entries.description: Japanese vulnerability countermeasure database (JVN iPedia) with MyJVN API (alerts, statistics).
entries.collaboration_route: Ask isec-jvndb@ipa.go.jp (contact per search result).
entries.recommended_use: Japanese-vendor vuln coverage pending terms.
entries.notes: Only search summaries read; WebFetch of /en/apis/ returned 404 to the fetcher. Terms PDF is Japanese and was not read; FAQ reportedly allows quoting with notification. Do not use until terms are read. API: MyJVN API (https://jvndb.jvn.jp/en/apis/).

entries.name: Kitsune Network Attack Dataset
entries.organisation: Ben-Gurion University of the Negev (Mirsky et al.)
entries.geographic_coverage: Lab: IP surveillance camera network and IoT network
entries.description: 9 attack captures (OS scan, fuzzing, video injection, ARP MitM, active wiretap, SSDP flood, SYN DoS, SSL renegotiation, Mirai) with Kitsune AfterImage feature vectors and PCAPs.
entries.records: 27,170,754 instances (UCI API num_instances)
entries.label_quality: Per-packet labels within each attack capture.
entries.known_limitations: Single small lab per attack. Labels are per capture scenario.
entries.attribution: Mirsky, Doitshman, Elovici, Shabtai, 'Kitsune: An Ensemble of Autoencoders for Online Network Intrusion Detection', NDSS 2018
entries.recommended_use: Openly licensed LAN attacks (ARP MitM, SSDP flood, Mirai) for edge and home-gateway detectors.
entries.notes: The UCI API returned license: null, but the rendered UCI dataset page states CC BY 4.0. The UCI listing does not name creators.

entries.name: LANL Comprehensive, Multi-Source Cyber-Security Events (2015)
entries.description: 58 consecutive days of de-identified authentication, process, internal DNS lookup and network flow events, plus labelled red-team events.
entries.records: 1,648,275,307 events in total for 12,425 users, 17,684 computers and 62,974 processes; about 12 GB compressed (dataset page)
entries.label_quality: Red-team events are labelled, but they are sparse and mostly authentication events. Everything else is unlabelled.
entries.known_limitations: DNS records hold only time, source and resolved computer (pseudonymised, no domain names). Very few positives.
entries.recommended_use: Commercially usable, real enterprise multi-source telemetry for SOC-style correlation and lateral-movement models.
entries.notes: CC0 waiver text is on the page. Of the real network datasets reviewed, this and the 2017 LANL set are the ones with an unambiguous commercial grant.

entries.name: LANL Unified Host and Network Dataset (2017)
entries.description: About 90 days of de-identified enterprise NetFlow (bidirectional events) and Windows host event logs, with consistent pseudonyms across both sources.
entries.label_quality: No attack labels. It is intended for anomaly and behaviour research.
entries.known_limitations: Unlabelled. Device and port names are pseudonymised.
entries.recommended_use: Large real enterprise benign baseline for flow-anomaly and false-positive calibration.
entries.notes: Licence text: 'To the extent possible under law, Los Alamos National Laboratory has waived all copyright and related or neighboring rights to Unified Host and Network DataSet.' Approved by the LANL Human Subject Research Review Board. Download needs an email and an intended-use statement (form only, no agreement).

entries.name: LOLBAS
entries.description: Living-off-the-land Windows binaries/scripts with abuse commands and ATT&CK mapping (YAML).
entries.recommended_use: Command-line detection features; GPL obligations on redistribution.
entries.notes: GitHub licence detection GPL-3.0. GPL allows commercial use; whether training/model outputs trigger copyleft is a legal question - training_use unclear.

entries.name: AIL framework (Analysis of Information Leaks)
entries.description: Open-source platform to crawl and analyse unstructured data (clear web, Tor, I2P, chats). Software, not a dataset.
entries.recommended_use: Optional upstream component for a backend research pipeline; licence-compatible with HookProbe AGPL.
entries.notes: CIRCL is the Computer Incident Response Center LUXEMBOURG (not Switzerland) - brief misattributed it.

entries.name: CIRCL hashlookup
entries.description: Known-file hash lookup (NSRL, Windows builds, Linux distro packages, CDNJS, Snap). Bloom filter of all SHA-1 (~700 MB, monthly) for offline checks.
entries.recommended_use: Offline allowlisting on edge devices via Bloom filter (privacy-preserving: no queries leave the device).
entries.notes: CIRCL is the Computer Incident Response Center LUXEMBOURG (not Switzerland) - brief misattributed it. Best-effort service.

entries.name: CIRCL MISP communities (private sector / partners)
entries.description: CIRCL operates several MISP instances for constituents and partners; open to organisations, CERTs, trusted researchers and security vendors subject to identity verification. Free of charge.
entries.collaboration_route: Apply via CIRCL contact with organisation, role, intended use and target community; identity verification required. Security vendors are an explicit applicant category. Non-Luxembourg eligibility not stated.
entries.recommended_use: Highest-value collaboration route in the CIRCL ecosystem for HookProbe as a security vendor; also a way to contribute anonymised edge sightings back.
entries.notes: CIRCL is the Computer Incident Response Center LUXEMBOURG (not Switzerland) - brief misattributed it.

entries.name: CIRCL OSINT Feed (MISP default feed)
entries.description: MISP-format feed of OSINT events curated by CIRCL; ~1,000 UUID-named JSON event files (1.5 KB-27 MB). Enabled by default in MISP installs.
entries.collaboration_route: info@circl.lu to confirm reuse terms for a commercial edge product
entries.recommended_use: Ingest via MISP or PyMISP feed parser; extract domain/hostname/url attributes for DNS blocklist candidates and training labels after confirming terms.
entries.notes: CIRCL is the Computer Incident Response Center LUXEMBOURG (not Switzerland) - brief misattributed it. No explicit copyright licence for feed contents found; TLP permits sharing but is not a licence. Directory listed, no files downloaded.

entries.name: CIRCL Open Data (phishing screenshots, BGP Ranking, AIL screenshots, Hugging Face datasets)
entries.description: Open datasets: >400 phishing site screenshots (circl-phishing-dataset-01), >37,000 dark-web screenshots, BGP Ranking per ASN, daily vulnerability dumps, operational statistics, and 14 Hugging Face datasets (mostly vulnerability scoring / CWE / ATT&CK mapping).
entries.recommended_use: BGP Ranking as an ASN-reputation feature for DNS/IP scoring; phishing screenshots for visual phishing classifier experiments.
entries.notes: CIRCL is the Computer Incident Response Center LUXEMBOURG (not Switzerland) - brief misattributed it. Individual HF dataset cards/licences not checked; no DNS or phishing dataset visible on HF org page.

entries.name: CIRCL Passive DNS
entries.description: REST passive DNS lookup by IP/hostname/domain, output in Passive DNS Common Output Format (JSON); v2 headers for rrtype filtering and pagination.
entries.collaboration_route: Request via CIRCL contact page stating affiliation and intended use; 'restricted to trusted partners in Luxembourg and abroad'.
entries.recommended_use: Enrichment/investigation of suspicious domains during labelling; not for bulk model training without explicit agreement.
entries.notes: CIRCL is the Computer Incident Response Center LUXEMBOURG (not Switzerland) - brief misattributed it.

entries.name: CIRCL Passive SSL
entries.description: Historical certificate-to-IP observations; JSON REST API.
entries.collaboration_route: Partners (security researchers, incident analysts) via CIRCL contact page.
entries.recommended_use: TLS/JA-style enrichment for flagged infrastructure.
entries.notes: CIRCL is the Computer Incident Response Center LUXEMBOURG (not Switzerland) - brief misattributed it.

entries.name: Vulnerability-Lookup (vulnerability.circl.lu)
entries.description: Aggregated vulnerability database (CVE, GCVE, national CERT and vendor sources) with API, RSS/Atom and daily NDJSON/JSON dumps; software is AGPL-3.0.
entries.collaboration_route: API key from CIRCL for higher rate limits; identify with a User-Agent containing a contact URL.
entries.recommended_use: CVE enrichment for device/firmware fingerprints seen at the edge; AGPL software aligns with HookProbe licensing.
entries.notes: CIRCL is the Computer Incident Response Center LUXEMBOURG (not Switzerland) - brief misattributed it. vulnerability.circl.lu itself did not resolve during research; per-source upstream licences (e.g. NVD, vendor feeds) may differ from CC BY - check api-policy.json. 2026-11-21: vulnerability.circl.lu resolves; /about lists each of ~99 upstream sources with its own licence (e.g. CVE Program, GitHub, OSV ecosystems CC BY 4.0; NVD public domain; OSV Ubuntu and Alpine CC BY-SA 4.0; several CSAF vendors and openEuler/Rocky with no licence shown). The CC BY label is NOT blanket: each dump is registered under its upstream source's own registry entry and licence.

entries.name: Malpedia
entries.description: Curated malware family inventory: names/aliases, actor mapping, references, YARA; samples restricted.
entries.collaboration_route: Invite-only trust group; ToS invites contact about 'possible alternative agreements'.
entries.recommended_use: Family-name normalisation only after an agreement.
entries.notes: 'The whole content of the website is released under ... CC BY-NC-SA 3.0'; non-public material treated TLP:AMBER. Same org as dgarchive (already in registry).

entries.name: Maltrail static trails
entries.description: Curated static trails (malware C2 domains/IPs/URLs, per-family) plus feed aggregation code.
entries.recommended_use: Static per-family trails as labelled IoCs; skip feed-aggregated trails.
entries.notes: Repo MIT; static trails are author-curated but cite public reports, dynamic trails pull third-party feeds - unclear for commercial training.

entries.name: MAWI Working Group Traffic Archive (WIDE backbone)
entries.geographic_coverage: Japan, WIDE transit links to upstream ISP (samplepoint-F), plus BBIX since 2023
entries.description: Daily backbone packet header traces (tcpdump, IPs scrambled with modified tcpdpriv) from 1999 to the present, plus long DITL traces. Real Internet background traffic.
entries.label_quality: Unlabelled. MAWILab provides anomaly labels up to 2024.
entries.known_limitations: Header-only, with payloads removed. Duplicated packets from 2015-05-28 to 2015-09-03. Heavy ICMP probing by the USC ANT project. Data gap from 2022-11-04 to 2022-12-15.
entries.recommended_use: Research-only background traffic for anomaly studies. Not for commercial model training.
entries.notes: The terms explicitly say research purposes only. A commercial product must not train on it without a separate agreement with WIDE.

entries.name: MAWILab
entries.organisation: Fukuda Lab, National Institute of Informatics (NII) with ENS Lyon
entries.geographic_coverage: Labels on MAWI samplepoints B and F
entries.description: Daily anomaly labels for MAWI traces, produced by combining several unsupervised detectors (PCA, Gamma, KL, Hough), with a taxonomy classification (v1.1, 2015). Available as XML and CSV.
entries.label_quality: Weak, detector-ensemble labels. The site says MAWILab is no longer maintained because the quality of its results and classification decreased over the years.
entries.known_limitations: Discontinued December 2024. Labels are not ground truth.
entries.attribution: Fontugne, Borgnat, Abry, Fukuda, 'MAWILab: Combining diverse anomaly detectors for automated anomaly labeling and performance benchmarking', ACM CoNEXT 2010
entries.recommended_use: Historical research benchmark only.
entries.notes: The MAWILab home page contains a stray, unrelated-looking contact email at the bottom. I ignored it and did not use it.

entries.name: Metasploit Framework
entries.description: Penetration-testing framework.
entries.recommended_use: authorised lab traffic generation for IDS eval
entries.notes: LICENSE is a Debian-format multi-licence file: core BSD-3, but bundled data includes GPL-2.0 (JtR), GPL-3.0 (SharpHound), LGPL-2.1 etc. Exploit code - high sensitivity.

entries.recommended_use: not a source for HookProbe; customer-side integration only

entries.name: Microsoft SimuLand
entries.description: Lab environment guides reproducing attack techniques for detection research.
entries.recommended_use: historical reference only
entries.notes: ARCHIVED (read-only) by owner on 2026-10-26; last commit 2023-03-09. Do not depend on it.

entries.name: MISP default feed list (feed-metadata/defaults.json)
entries.description: Index of 108 default OSINT feeds preconfigured in MISP (abuse.ch, CIRCL OSINT, Botvrij, ET, IPsum, Threatview, CERT-PL, etc.).

entries.name: botvrij.eu OSINT feed
entries.description: IoCs extracted from public blogs/PDF reports, ~6-month retention; MISP OSINT feed and flat lists.
entries.recommended_use: Internal live enrichment; no resale.

Shipping inside a paid product may count as resale - treat commercial as unclear. Listed in MISP default feeds (misp-default-feeds) but not as its own registry entry.

entries.name: MISP Galaxy clusters
entries.description: Curated JSON knowledge base: threat actors, malware families, tools, ransomware, sectors, ATT&CK mappings, etc.

entries.name: MISP Taxonomies
entries.description: Machine-readable classification vocabularies (TLP, PAP, ENISA, incident types, etc.).
entries.recommended_use: Label schema for SOC triage outputs.

entries.name: MISP Warninglists
entries.description: Lists of known benign/false-positive indicators (cloud ranges, top domains, public DNS resolvers, CDN, RFC1918, etc.).

HookProbe embedding = commercial. Developer licence excludes commercial/production use (search snippet).

entries.description: 'Don't Route Or Peer' lists of netblocks/ASNs controlled by criminals; EDROP merged into DROP on 2024-04-10.

entries.attribution: If used in a product, credit The Spamhaus Project and keep the date and © text with the file/data.

Classified RESTRICTED because no open licence, though device redistribution in product appears permitted with credit.

entries.name: Stratosphere / Malware Capture Facility Project captures (CTU-Malware-Capture-Botnet-*, Normal, Mixed)
entries.description: Long-running catalogue of individual malware execution captures, plus normal and mixed captures. Per-capture PCAPs, Argus/Zeek flows and labels, and often the malware sample (password 'infected').
entries.label_quality: Varies per capture. Many captures are labelled only at host or capture level.
entries.known_limitations: Heterogeneous formats and labels. Some PCAPs are withheld for privacy. Contains live malware.
entries.recommended_use: Supplementary C2 and malware network-behaviour samples. Confirm the licence with Stratosphere before commercial training.
entries.notes: FAQ text: 'You do not need to ask permission from us to use our datasets as long as you cite the datasets appropriately'. This is permissive but not a formal licence. The only explicit CC-BY statement found covers CTU-13. The MCFP index returned no parseable listing to curl.

entries.description: Granular cloud attack technique emulation.

entries.notes: Last push 2026-11-17.

entries.name: TON_IoT datasets
entries.organisation: UNSW Canberra (Cyber Range and IoT Labs)
entries.description: Heterogeneous Industry 4.0 / IoT / IIoT data: telemetry from more than 10 IoT/IIoT sensors, Windows 7/10 and Ubuntu 14/18 audit traces, and network traffic (PCAP and Zeek CSV). Attacks include DoS, DDoS, ransomware, scanning, injection, XSS and backdoor.
entries.label_quality: Testbed ground truth. I found no audit.
entries.known_limitations: Synthetic testbed.
entries.attribution: cite the eight papers listed on the TON_IoT page
entries.recommended_use: IoT and multi-source correlation research. Commercial use only after written permission.
entries.notes: The download link ('HERE') is a UNSW SharePoint link and was not extracted. Funded by ARDC. Of the UNSW sets, this has the most commercially permissive wording ('allowable after asking'), but it still needs explicit permission.

entries.name: Tor Metrics CollecTor (exit lists, relay descriptors)

entries.recommended_use: Tor-exit labelling of flows; anonymiser features.

entries.name: DNS tunnelling dataset (Tu, Liu, Sun, Computers & Security 2023)
entries.organisation: Tianjin University Trusted Software Lab with an enterprise security lab
entries.geographic_coverage: Campus lab and one enterprise office network
entries.description: PCAP dataset. Benign DNS from browsing subdomains of the Alexa top 1K (found via certificate transparency) plus filtered lab DNS. Malicious traffic from 8 tunnel tools (iodine, dnscat2, dns2tcp, ozymandns, dnshell, Cobalt Strike, DET, dnsexfiltrator). Generalisation set uses enterprise benign DNS and 150 real post-exploitation commands over tunnels.
entries.records: Repo size about 397 MB (GitHub API size 397,076 KB). Packet counts not read.
entries.label_quality: Labels come from the generating tool. A generalisation test set is included. Non-DNS packets must be filtered (README).
entries.known_limitations: No licence. Base malicious set is mostly heartbeat packets (README).
entries.attribution: Tu, Liu, Sun, 'DNS tunnelling detection by fusing encoding feature and behavioral feature', Computers & Security 132 (2023)
entries.recommended_use: Evaluation and research reference only. Its broad tool coverage, including Cobalt Strike DNS, makes it a strong test set.
entries.notes: With no licence, default copyright applies (all rights reserved). The README asks only for citation. The enterprise benign PCAPs may contain internal hostnames; the README says the IPs are from an isolated network.

entries.name: Ubuntu Security Notices (USN) in OSV format
entries.description: Ubuntu USNs and CVE records in OSV JSON.
entries.recommended_use: Ubuntu package vuln matching; share-alike applies to redistributed adaptations.
entries.notes: README '## LICENSE': 'licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License'. Share-alike: keep a derived redistributed dataset under CC BY-SA; model-weight status under SA is a legal question - flag to counsel.

entries.name: UGR'16
entries.organisation: Network Engineering & Security Group (NESG), University of Granada
entries.description: About 4 months of real anonymised NetFlow v9 from a Spanish ISP. Calibration set (Mar-Jun 2016) and test set (Jul-Aug 2016) with injected synthetic attacks (DoS, scans, botnet) plus detected real anomalies (spam, SSH scans, UDP scans).
entries.records: Packed size 236 GB (COMIDDS catalogue; not read on the original page)
entries.label_quality: Weak. Real flows are labelled 'background', which is not guaranteed benign, and flagged anomalies are not necessarily real attacks (per COMIDDS summary of the authors).
entries.known_limitations: Real ISP data, so background traffic is unlabelled. Attacks are injected synthetically.
entries.attribution: Maciá-Fernández et al., 'UGR'16: A new dataset for the evaluation of cyclostationarity-based network IDSs', Computers & Security 73 (2018)
entries.recommended_use: Realistic ISP background traffic for anomaly detection and false-positive calibration, if licence terms are confirmed.
entries.notes: The original site (nesg.ugr.es) returned HTTP 403 to both curl and WebFetch, so no licence text was read. The UGR repository record of the paper is CC BY-NC-ND 3.0 ES, but that covers the article, not the data. Derived feature data by Camacho et al. (codas.ugr.es) is reported as CC BY-NC (search result, unverified). Assume non-commercial until confirmed.

entries.name: Cambridge Cybercrime Centre datasets
entries.description: Datasets incl. phishing emails (since 2005), .com/.net domain registration archive since 2009 (raw may not be shareable), spam (Abusix feed since 2020), reflected-DDoS victim data (>4 trillion packets), Mirai scans, underground forums, investment-scam URLs (>150k).
entries.collaboration_route: Email datarequest AT cambridgecybercrime.uk with institution agreement wording, lead researcher, project description; institution signs 1-year agreement. Commercial use significantly restricted - best via an academic partner (e.g. UPB).
entries.recommended_use: Research-only evaluation via a university partner; not for product training.

entries.name: CiSP - Cyber Security Information Sharing Partnership
entries.description: Free secure sharing platform; membership requires NCSC approval and (per T&Cs v5.0) UK-registered company or entity administering a UK network; possible ROCU vetting.
entries.collaboration_route: Not available to a Romanian-only entity; would require a UK-registered subsidiary and sponsor.
entries.recommended_use: Ignore unless a UK entity is created.
entries.notes: Eligibility from search snippet of UK CISP Terms and Conditions v5.0; page not fetched.

entries.name: NCSC UK Annual Review 2026 - Active Cyber Defence
entries.description: Published 3 Nov 2026: 1.6M+ commodity campaigns disrupted, 30,000 GOV.UK-impersonating phishing attacks taken down (median 90 min), UK share of global phishing 1.06% (Jun 2026), 52,000+ vulnerability notifications.
entries.recommended_use: Benchmark for takedown/phishing metrics; no raw data.
entries.notes: No data download. UK PDNS (Protective DNS) and Early Warning are UK-eligibility services; not available to a Romanian company (eligibility not re-verified).

entries.name: NCSC UK GitHub (ukncsc)
entries.description: Guidance and tooling repos: Logging Made Easy (archived, Apache-2.0), Device Security Guidance Configuration Packs (Apache-2.0, updated Mar 2026), zero-trust-architecture principles, terraform-aws-mtasts, stix-cvebuilder. No IOC feeds.
entries.recommended_use: Hardening baselines for HookProbe appliance; MTA-STS patterns.

entries.name: UMUDGA (University of Murcia DGA Dataset)
entries.description: Over 30 million algorithmically generated domains from 50 malware DGA families, with a precomputed lexical and NLP feature set (ARFF/CSV). Companion code is on GitHub.
entries.records: Over 30 million labelled AGDs (dataset description via search snippet; DiB article)
entries.label_quality: Algorithmic ground truth (generated domains), with family labels.
entries.known_limitations: Generated, not observed in the wild. Families date to 2020. Benign class composition not verified.
entries.attribution: MIT notice; cite Zago, Gil Pérez, Martínez Pérez, UMUDGA, Data in Brief 2020, doi:10.1016/j.dib.2020.105400 (dataset doi:10.17632/y8ph45msv8.1)
entries.recommended_use: Primary commercially usable DGA training corpus for the DNS edge detector.
entries.notes: The Mendeley page licence field reads MIT (both in the rendered HTML and in JSON-LD). The GitHub code repo is also MIT. The Zenodo DOI release 10.5281/zenodo.3618221 (code) shows 'other-open'. The Data in Brief article links CC BY 4.0 for the article itself. The record count comes from the search snippet of the Mendeley description, not a file count.

entries.name: Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 timely threat intel (IOC repo)
entries.description: IOC files accompanying Unit 42 social media posts.
entries.recommended_use: IOC enrichment / eval; GPL on data makes training status unclear
entries.notes: Active (last push 2026-11-17). Unstructured text; GPL-3.0 applied to data is unusual - shipping in proprietary images triggers GPL obligations (compatible with AGPL edition). Older pan-unit42/iocs repo also referenced by MISP feeds (licence not checked).

entries.name: UNSW-NB15
entries.description: Hybrid real-normal and synthetic-attack traffic from IXIA PerfectStorm. 9 attack families (Fuzzers, Analysis, Backdoors, DoS, Exploits, Generic, Reconnaissance, Shellcode, Worms). 49 Argus/Bro features. 100 GB of PCAPs.
entries.records: 2,540,044 records in 4 CSVs; training set 175,341 and testing set 82,332 records (UNSW-NB15 page)
entries.label_quality: Ground truth from the IXIA attack generator. Known issues in the literature include feature leakage (e.g. TTL fields) and class overlap. I did not verify these claims here.
entries.known_limitations: Synthetic attack traffic. The 'Generic' and 'Exploits' classes are coarse.
entries.attribution: cite the five papers listed on the page, incl. Moustafa & Slay, 'UNSW-NB15: a comprehensive data set for network intrusion detection systems', MilCIS 2015
entries.recommended_use: Academic benchmark only unless a commercial agreement is signed with Dr Nour Moustafa.
entries.notes: Kaggle re-upload mrwellsdavid/unsw-nb15 shows licence 'Unknown'. CIC also publishes a CICFlowMeter re-extraction (CIC-UNSW-NB15, https://www.unb.ca/cic/datasets/cic-unsw-nb15.html). Its derived data is still bound by UNSW's commercial restriction.

entries.name: UQ NetFlow NIDS datasets (NF-UNSW-NB15, NF-ToN-IoT, NF-BoT-IoT, NF-CSE-CIC-IDS2018, NF-UQ-NIDS; v1/v2/v3)
entries.organisation: University of Queensland (Portmann, Sarhan, Layeghy, Luay) with UNSW (Moustafa)
entries.description: Common NetFlow feature sets (v1 has 12 features, v2 has 43, v3 has 53 with temporal features) re-extracted from UNSW-NB15, ToN-IoT, BoT-IoT and CSE-CIC-IDS2018, plus the merged NF-UQ-NIDS. Useful for cross-dataset generalisation.
entries.records: NF-UNSW-NB15-v3: 2,365,424 flows, 127,639 (5.4%) attacks (UQ page); NF-UNSW-NB15-v2: 2,390,275 flows
entries.label_quality: Inherits the source labels, including CSE-CIC-IDS2018 errors. Attack categories were merged in NF-UQ-NIDS.
entries.known_limitations: Derived data. NetFlow matches what an edge router can export, which is useful.
entries.attribution: Sarhan, Layeghy, Moustafa, Portmann, 'NetFlow Datasets for Machine Learning-Based NIDS', BDTA/WiCON 2020; Luay et al. 2025 (v3)
entries.recommended_use: Best feature format match for router NetFlow/IPFIX. Licence follows the sources: UNSW-derived parts need UNSW agreement, CIC-derived parts follow CIC terms.
entries.notes: Derived works cannot loosen the source terms, so UNSW-derived subsets keep UNSW's 'commercial use should be agreed' condition.
